name: Breedon Group plc
executive_summary: Breedon Group plc is a vertically integrated construction materials business spanning Great Britain, Ireland and the United States, with long-life mineral reserves, two UK cement plants, and a progressive cash-return policy. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy on cheapness (P/B ~0.9, EV/EBITDA ~7.2), an ~11.5% FCF yield, and a ~4.5% dividend yield, with nine of 22 models passing across cheapness, dividend, GARP and risk families. Filings confirm resilient cash generation and covenant headroom, but earnings quality is cyclically constrained: Great Britain volumes are in a multi-year downturn, ROIC is 7.0–7.8% versus management’s 10% medium-term target, and leverage has risen with US M&A. The central debate is whether geographic diversification (Ireland, US infrastructure) and self-help can sustain cash returns through a prolonged UK construction trough, or whether further M&A and cyclical weakness will keep returns below cost of capital.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Breedon offers a rare combination in UK basic materials: tangible asset backing, statutory net assets of £1,197m at 31 December 2025, and filing-verified free cash flow of £133.2m in FY2025 (48% FCF conversion), supporting a 15.0p full-year dividend (47% payout). The screen’s strong-buy signal (composite 81%, conviction persistent for 12 weeks) is grounded in deep value and cash-return metrics rather than earnings momentum: statutory basic EPS fell to 24.2p in 2025 from 28.1p, yet the business passed Financial Health, Earnings Quality, FCF Yield, Dividend Growth and Composite Value models with full data quality (20/20 metrics).

Business quality supports the signal at the balance-sheet level. Breedon holds 1.5–1.7bn tonnes of mineral reserves, operates as the largest British-based domestic cement manufacturer, and has extended RCF maturity to July 2029 (subsequently July 2030 post-H1 2026) alongside long-dated USPP notes. Management delivered over £20m of operational savings in 2025, maintained underlying EBITDA margins near 16% group-wide despite LFL revenue decline, and reduced covenant leverage from a H1 2025 peak of 2.2x to 1.8x at year-end. The investment case is therefore “quality cyclical at a discount”: not a growth compounder today, but a cash-generative, asset-heavy platform priced for continued UK weakness, with Ireland and US bolt-ons providing partial offset and optionality when GB volumes recover.
financial_review:
Primary source: UK RNS filings (Final Results, 11 March 2026; Interim Results 2026, 29 July 2026; trading updates). The filings index contains annual and interim coverage; one formal interim release (H1 2026) is present, with H1 2025 comparatives restated inside that document. No separate H1 2025 interim filing body is indexed.

Annual results — year ended 31 December 2025 (Final Results RNS, 11 March 2026)

| Metric | 2025 | 2024 | Change |
|--------|------|------|--------|
| Revenue | £1,713.8m | £1,576.3m | +9% (LFL −3%) |
| Underlying EBITDA | £278.8m | £269.9m | +3% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 16.3% | 17.1% | −80bps |
| Statutory PBT | £105.3m | £125.4m | −16% |
| Underlying PBT | £140.2m | £150.8m | −7% |
| Basic EPS (statutory) | 24.2p | 28.1p | −14% |
| Adjusted underlying basic EPS | 31.8p | 34.4p | −8% |
| Free cash flow | £133.2m | £114.1m | +17% |
| FCF conversion | 48% | 42% | +600bps |
| Net debt (incl. IFRS 16) | £527.3m | £405.3m | +30% |
| Covenant leverage | 1.8x | 1.4x | +0.4x |
| ROIC (post-tax) | 7.8% | 9.0% | −120bps |
| Dividend per share | 15.0p | 14.5p | +3% |

Revenue growth was acquisition-led (Lionmark, full-year BMC); organic pressure came from a fourth consecutive year of declining GB volumes, with ready-mixed concrete at historically low levels. Underlying EBITDA still rose 3% on cost discipline. Statutory profit was weighed down by higher amortisation of acquired intangibles (£25.3m non-underlying), increased finance costs (£29.7m), and cement decarbonisation spend. Cash performance was the standout: record post-Covid FCF, with net capex of £110.5m (106% of depreciation). Liquidity at year-end exceeded £245m (undrawn RCF >£130m plus cash >£115m). Impairment testing retained headroom in all three CGUs, including additional GB sensitivities.

Segmental FY2025 underlying EBITDA: GB £185.2m (−4%), Ireland £64.3m (−7%), US £42.8m (+73%, Lionmark-inclusive).

Interim results — six months ended 30 June 2026 (Interim Results RNS, 29 July 2026)

| Metric | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | £857.9m | £815.9m | +5% (LFL +3%) |
| Underlying EBITDA | £115.5m | £115.0m | Flat (LFL +1%) |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 13.5% | 14.1% | −60bps |
| Statutory PBT | £26.7m | £34.9m | −16% |
| Adjusted underlying basic EPS | 9.4p | 11.2p | −16% |
| Interim dividend | 5.00p | 4.75p | +5% |
| Net debt | £690.5m | £648.1m | +7% |
| Covenant leverage | 2.1x | 2.2x | −0.1x |
| ROIC (LTM) | 7.0% | 7.8% | −80bps |
| H1 free cash flow | (£14.6m) | (£25.0m) | Improved |

H1 2026 showed geographic divergence: Ireland revenue +12% (LFL +9%), US +20% (LFL +13%, underlying EBITDA LFL +14%), GB flat revenue with underlying EBITDA −3%. M&A deployed £110m (Falling Springs ~£90m EV, Booth, Burfordville). H1 FCF outflow reflected seasonal working capital (£64.8m build); management guided to second-half deleveraging. FY2026 underlying EBITDA guidance maintained in line with consensus (~£280m). Interest cover (LTM to June 2026) was 13.5x versus a 3.5x covenant minimum; leverage covenant threshold is 3.0x.

Trading updates (filings)

- Trading Update to 31 October 2025 (20 November 2025): ten-month revenue +9% reported, −3% LFL; FY2025 underlying EBITDA guided £275–280m; covenant leverage expected to reduce from H1 peak.
- AGM Trading Update (29 April 2026): Q1 revenue +5% (+2% LFL); US and Ireland encouraging, GB softer on residential ready-mix.

Yahoo fallback

Filings provide sufficient figures for this review. Yahoo `financials_annual.json` (as at 4 September 2026) is broadly consistent with statutory FY2025 revenue (£1,713.8m), net income (£83.8m), and FCF (£105.8m per Yahoo vs £133.2m per filing definition — the filing explicitly adjusts FCF for major projects and acquisition cash; screen FCF of £133.2m aligns with the RNS non-GAAP definition). Yahoo quarterly cashflow is empty (TTM suppressed); no Yahoo figures were required for core trends.

Trend summary

Revenue has grown reported mid/high single digits on M&A, but LFL revenue was negative in FY2025 and only modestly positive in H1 2026. Margins are resilient but compressing. Balance-sheet leverage has risen materially (net debt +£122m YoY at FY2025; +£163m H1 2026 net debt increase including acquisitions) yet remains inside the 1–2x target range at year-end and below the 3.0x covenant at H1 2026 (2.1x). Cash conversion and dividend growth remain strengths; ROIC and statutory EPS are weaknesses pending a GB volume inflection.
risks_and_flags:
Cyclical exposure dominates. Filings describe GB ready-mixed concrete volumes declining for a fifth consecutive year in 2026, with residential new-build particularly weak; pricing pressure intensified after four years of volume decline. Enquiry levels are elevated but conversion to orders remains delayed — a classic late-cycle pattern that screens may underweight.

Leverage and M&A integration. Lionmark (US$238m EV, March 2025), Falling Springs (US$120m, May/June 2026) and Booth (Ireland) have lifted net debt and amortisation of acquired intangibles (£10.9m in H1 2026 alone). Pro-forma leverage was guided at 2.0x post-Falling Springs. ROIC at 7.0–7.8% sits below management’s 10% medium-term target, reflecting acquisition dilution and subdued profitability — a red flag for capital allocation quality if M&A continues without organic recovery.

Regulatory and climate. Breedon flags UK/EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism implementation (2026/2027), uneven carbon regulation, high UK energy costs, and cement import competition. Peak Cluster CCS requires >£20m investment over three years pre-FID; cement decarbonisation costs were £5.8m in FY2025. These are structural, not transient.

Operational and financial covenant language is reassuring but not risk-free. Going concern statements (annual and interim) cite comfortable covenant compliance, liquidity, and a “severe but plausible” downside (5–10% revenue reduction) retaining headroom. Borrowing facilities (£400m RCF to 2030; ~£363m USPP) remain compliant; interest cover 13.5x. However, H1 2026 net debt of £690.5m at 2.1x leverage sits at the upper end of the 1–2x management target, with H1 FCF negative and £110m acquisition spend — deleveraging in H2 is assumed, not yet delivered.

Other filing-identified principal risks: acquisitions/capex execution, land and mineral permitting, health and safety, IT/cyber, supply-chain/input costs (Middle East conflict cited as monitored; minimal direct impact to date per H1 2026), and market/competition. Pension risk is not prominently quantified in the indexed filing extracts reviewed.

RiskTags: cyclical, regulatory, leverage, competitive, other
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate and RNS-heavy, with sell-side aggregator repetition; several headline matches are irrelevant (e.g. “Home and Away” soap spoilers).

Material items from the news manifest and aligned RNS:

- “Breedon Wins Cross-Party MP Support for Back British Cement Campaign” (TipRanks, 3 September 2026) — political advocacy for domestic cement ahead of CBAM; complements RNS “MPs Back British Cement” (3 September 2026).
- “Breedon Steps Up Back British Cement Campaign as UK Output Hits Historic Lows” (TipRanks, 11 August 2026) — strategic/regulatory positioning.
- H1 2026 results cluster (29 July 2026): “BREE: Revenue up 5% with strong US and Ireland growth; GB remains challenged; dividend raised 5%” (TradingView); “Breedon Group H1 Earnings Call Highlights” (Yahoo Finance) — revenue +5%, flat underlying EBITDA, dividend +5%.
- “Breedon Group Names Louis Eperjesi as Non-Executive Director Starting Early 2027” (Kalkine Media, 29 July 2026) — board refresh alongside interim results.
- “Breedon Group's (BREE) Buy Rating Reiterated at Berenberg Bank / Deutsche Bank” (MarketBeat, 30–31 July 2026) — supportive sell-side tone post-results.
- Falling Springs acquisition (9 June 2026 RNS; limited third-party coverage) — US$120m bolt-on near St Louis.
- FY2025 results (11 March 2026): “Breedon struggles to escape UK construction gloom” (Investors’ Chronicle, 11 March 2026) — balanced media framing of UK weakness versus cash generation.
- Analyst narrative pieces (Yahoo Finance, March–June 2026) note fair-value/target resets (e.g. toward ~£4.05–£4.50 vs higher prior anchors) — sentiment cooling despite constructive ratings.
- Dividend-focused articles around ex-dividend (May 2026) — routine, not strategic.

Overall: news flow confirms the filing narrative (GB weak, US/Ireland offset, M&A active, regulatory campaign on cement) rather than introducing new financial data. Third-party fundamental coverage is thin beyond results-day syndication.
research_rationale: Filings corroborate the screen’s value and cash-return case—sub-book valuation, strong FY2025 FCF, progressive dividend and covenant headroom—but cyclical GB weakness, M&A-driven leverage and sub-target ROIC temper outright strong-buy conviction pending a UK volume inflection.

meta_reflection.observation: Filings-first order is adequate in principle for BREE.L: a genuine 11 Mar 2026 Final Results (eddaa504dfb0ee94, priority 120), 23 Mar 2025 Annual Report + AGM notice (af6f746de7cb473b), 29 Jul 2026 Interim results (12bf5ad24805dc03), Nov 2025 Trading Update, and 29 Apr 2026 AGM Trading Update all exist with has_body=true. It is not adequate in practice: period_coverage annual=12 / interim=1 / trading_update=2 counts Notice of Annual Results, Live IMC presentation, Backing British Cement, a PDMR row, two Google News “Across The Markets: Breedon, Quilter, Games Workshop” items, and CH initial/2023–24 accounts as annual. The June 2026 Acquisition — first-class capital allocation — is period=other / priority 0, ranked with TVR/holdings. yahoo_quarterly_cashflow sits on the ladder but is empty (expected for a UK half-year reporter) while alternate_news and ir_presentation_metrics are absent. filings_index.body_path values point at docs/data/research/BREE.L or output/research/BREE.L rather than this trial tree.

The screen emits strong_buy (9/22, four families, composite 0.815 vs sector 0.766) as a 12-week persistent print while quality is the missing family, ROE is 6.9%, NI/EPS have declined for three years, net debt has roughly quadrupled since FY2023, and cyclical_exposure_detected is false on a GB heavyside materials name. Snapshot research_* is already pre-seeded “Accumulate, Medium risk” with the action_note duplicated five times, conviction_score is 0.882 while the summary string says Conviction 63%, failed_models=[] despite 13 models not passing, and trade_plan is null while the summary cites £327-class limits. Director–worker qualitative veto is doing the work a cyclical + FCF-definition + unit-hygiene overlay should have done before a verify-before-trade memo is commissioned.

Mandatory annual+interim summarize_filing_body plus news+screen+gap consumes the five-task cap even when the right FY Final Results and H1 bodies are chosen. There is no type or period flag for trading_update (Nov 2025 / Apr 2026 AGM TU), acquisition, rns_cluster (PDMR/TVR/holdings), campaign_rns (Back British Cement), or catalog_period_mismatch (Google News / IMC / notice tagged annual). gap_inventory can only list that the Annual Report, CH 2026 group accounts, June Acquisition, and both trading updates were dropped — it cannot assign them.

weeks_at_signal=12 / stability=persistent / signal_since 2026-08-02 already mark a stale-to-mid-life print, but there is no watch schema for: a typical autumn 2026 trading update (catalog has 20 Nov 2025 TU only), GB volume inflection vs H1 “challenged” language, H1-implied FY2026 guidance, net-debt path after 481m Yahoo net debt plus the unread June acquisition, FCF 133.2m vs 105.8m vs dividend cash 51.1m, Back British Cement / UK cement-output policy, analyst PT drift £5.00→£4.05, or pence-vs-pounds limit hygiene. RSI 43 + price>50>200 timing=neutral is not a substitute. News freshness reaches 3 Sep; filings_index fetched 17:27Z on 4 Sep — a one-day news stall, not a filings stall. Home and Away “Bree” soap collisions are in the manifest.

A generic FINANCIAL REVIEW / RISKS split will blend Yahoo GBP statutory with company underlying EBITDA/FCF and will not force GB vs Ireland vs US, volume vs price/mix, FCF 133.2m vs 105.8m vs cash dividends 51.1m, net debt 122m→481m plus June M&A, LSE pence vs £327 limit-string vs £4.05–£5.00 Street targets, or statutory vs underlying. Without GEO/PRODUCT MIX, CAPITAL FRAME (capex + M&A + dividend cover + covenants), GUIDANCE PATH (FY Mar → AGM TU Apr → H1 Jul → missing autumn TU), POLICY/CEMENT (Back British Cement vs structural GB decline), and UNIT HYGIENE (pence vs pounds, Yahoo cash 115.5m vs cash-flow end-cash 71.6m) slots, workers will treat Kalkine regeneration pairings, DirectorsTalk upside SEO, and Home and Away hits as colour. Director catalog pass can form these questions without drafting the memo.
